newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cert coffee stocks fall to new all-time low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cert coffee stocks fall to new all-time low.

text.p: U.S. certified coffee stocks continued to decline, falling by 743 60-kg bags in the week ended November 1, to 804 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Monday.
The latest drawdown puts the exchange cache at its lowest level since the CSCE began tracking inventories in 1980.
No coffee was pending grading or recertification, the exchange said.
The 48 percent drop in stocks was generally in line with expectations, traders said. With no stocks pending grading a week ago, traders had anticipated a further drawdown.
"The trend is set. There is no spot coffee," one dealer said.
Traders said the draw may prove supportive to the nearby December/March switch -- a barometer of near-term availability -- which dipped Monday to 10.70 cents from 10.80 cents at the close Friday.
But with 15 days remaining until December enters its month-long notice period, traders said the flow of coffee -- particularly from Mexico and Colombia -- could pressure prices.
The December contract, which expires December 18, had 10,912 lots open interest as of Friday, or the equivalent to about 2.7 million bags of coffee.
